newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Bank Leumi raised to buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Bank Leumi raised to buy.

text.p: UBS Global Research has raised its rating for Israel's Bank Leumi to buy from hold, UBS said in a report released on Sunday.

Analyst Daniel Carasso said Leumi's profitability and return on equity (ROE) should show a big improvement in 1996 and 1997. He estimated earnings per share would grow to 0.559 shekel in 1997 and 0.694 shekel in 1998 from an estimated 0.433 shekel last year and 0.320 shekel in 1995.
ROE, he said, was set to grow to 8.1 percent in 1996 from 6.3 percent in 1995. In 1997, he forecast, ROE would reach 10.1 percent.
"Higher commissions income and greater fund management income in a healthy (stock market) environment would increase earnings by 0.22 shekel a share, or about 55 percent," Carasso added.

He cited several factors for the improvement in Leumi's performance, among them a successful cost-reduction programme and an end to losses at its New York operation. He noted that Leumi should receive about 750 million shekels in cash and a 400 million shekel capital gain from its sale of shares in Africa Israel Investments and Migdal insurance.
The report said Leumi's shares were trading cheaply based on a price of 4.96 shekels a share. On Sunday, Leumi closed at 4.74 shekels.

Based on UBS's estimates, the bank is valued at just under nine times 1997 earnings, while European banks of similar quality are trading at 10 to 16 times. Carasso added that Leumi is trading at a bigger discount to book value than comparable European banks.
